qualification.reason: The document is a Request for Proposals issued by the City of Providence for parking signs, posts, and related materials, including submission deadline, scope of work, evaluation criteria, and bid forms.

quotes.quote: REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS
Item Description:  PARKING SIGNS, PARKING SIGN POSTS, AND RELATED PARKING ADMINISTRATION MATERIALS – ONE-YEAR CONTRACT WITH TWO ONE-YEAR RENEWAL OPTIONS

The City of Providence Department of Public Works, Parking Administration Division, seeks competitive bids from qualified manufacturers and distributors for the furnishing and delivery of parking regulatory signs, parking sign posts, mounting hardware, parking control devices, and related materials on an as-needed basis under a firm fixed unit price requirements contract.
Bids may be submitted up to 2:15 P.M. on the above meeting date at the Department of the City Clerk.

findings.title: Certificate of Good Standing Required
findings.fact: Bidders must be able to provide a Certificate of Good Standing with the Rhode Island Secretary of State upon request.

quotes.quote: Certificate of Good Standing with the Rhode Island Secretary of State.

findings.title: Proof of Insurance Required
findings.fact: Bidders must be able to provide proof of insurance upon request.

quotes.quote: Proof of Insurance.

findings.title: Business Tax ID Required After Award
findings.fact: Business Tax ID will be requested after an award is approved by the Board of Contract and Supply.

quotes.quote: Business Tax ID will be requested after an award is approved by the Board of Contract and Supply.

findings.title: Delivery Timeframes
findings.fact: Standard stock items must be delivered within five business days; custom signs within ten business days; emergency orders within twenty-four hours.

quotes.quote: Standard stock items shall be delivered within five business days. Custom signs shall be delivered within ten business days. Emergency orders shall be delivered within twenty-four hours whenever practicable.

findings.title: Proof Submission Timeframe
findings.fact: The Contractor shall prepare electronic proofs in PDF format within 48 hours.

quotes.quote: The Contractor shall prepare electronic proofs in PDF format within 48 hours and shall not begin production until written City approval.

findings.title: Product Discontinuation Notice
findings.fact: The Contractor must notify the City within 30 days of product discontinuation.

quotes.quote: In case of product discontinuation, the Contractor will notify the City within 30 days, recommend replacements, and maintain pricing whenever possible.

findings.title: Evaluation of Optional Installation Services
findings.fact: Pricing for installation services is evaluated separately from the base bid and does not affect determination of lowest bidder for materials.

quotes.quote: Pricing for installation services shall be evaluated separately from the base bid and shall not affect the determination of the lowest responsive and responsible bidder for the materials portion of the solicitation unless otherwise stated in the Bid Form.

findings.title: Estimated Quantities for Bid Evaluation
findings.fact: Estimated quantities are provided solely for bid evaluation and are not guaranteed.

quotes.quote: Estimated quantities are provided solely for bid evaluation.

findings.title: Right to Request Additional Information
findings.fact: The City reserves the right to request clarifications, product literature, samples, and additional information prior to award.

quotes.quote: The City reserves the right to request clarifications, product literature, samples, and additional information prior to award, waive minor informalities, reject any or all bids, and determine the bid most advantageous to the City.

findings.title: Cash discounts not considered in determining lowest responsible bidder
findings.fact: In determining the lowest responsible bidder, cash discounts based on preferable payment terms will not be considered.

quotes.quote: In determining the lowest responsible bidder, cash discounts based on preferable payment terms will not be considered.

findings.title: Right to award to one bidder or split award when prices are the same
findings.fact: Where prices are the same, the Board of Contract and Supply reserves the right to award to one bidder, or to split the award.

quotes.quote: Where prices are the same, the Board of Contract and Supply reserves the right to award to one bidder, or to split the award.

findings.title: Bids may be submitted on an 'equal in quality' basis
findings.fact: Bids may be submitted on an 'equal in quality' basis. The City reserves the right to decide equality. Bidders must indicate brand or the make being offered and submit detailed specifications if other than brand requested.

quotes.quote: Bids may be submitted on an “equal in quality” basis. The City reserves the right to decide equality. Bidders must indicate brand or the make being offered and submit detailed specifications if other than brand requested.

findings.title: Unit price governs in case of error in extension of prices
findings.fact: In case of error in the extension of prices quoted, the unit price will govern.

quotes.quote: In case of error in the extension of prices quoted, the unit price will govern.

findings.title: Delivery dates must be shown in the bid
findings.fact: Delivery dates must be shown in the bid. If no delivery date is specified, it will be assumed that an immediate delivery from stock will be made.

quotes.quote: Delivery dates must be shown in the bid. If no delivery date is specified, it will be assumed that an immediate delivery from stock will be made.

findings.title: Renewal Price Adjustment Cap
findings.fact: Renewal price adjustments are limited to the lesser of CPI-U increase or 3%.

quotes.quote: Renewal price adjustments may be requested only during renewal periods and shall not exceed the lesser of the annual CPI-U increase or three percent, supported by documentation.

findings.title: Warranty Requirement
findings.fact: Contractor must provide a minimum 10-year manufacturer's warranty covering specified defects.

quotes.quote: Provide a minimum ten-year manufacturer's warranty covering reflectivity, delamination, peeling, cracking, corrosion, fading, adhesive failure, ink failure, and manufacturing defects.

findings.title: Tax Exemption
findings.fact: Prices quoted must not include Federal Excise Taxes or Rhode Island Sales Tax as the City is exempt.

quotes.quote: As the City of Providence is exempt from the payment of Federal Excise Taxes and Rhode Island Sales Tax, prices quoted are not to include these taxes.

findings.title: No Assignment Without Consent
findings.fact: Contractor cannot assign or underlet the contract without prior written consent of the City Purchasing Director.

quotes.quote: The contractor will NOT be permitted to: a) assign or underlet the contract, or b) assign either legally or equitably any monies or any claim thereto without the previous written consent of the City Purchasing Director.

findings.title: No Interest on Overdue Payments
findings.fact: The City shall not be obligated to pay interest on any overdue invoice or payment.

quotes.quote: In no circumstances shall the City be obligated to pay or shall you be entitled to receive interest on any overdue invoice or payment.

findings.title: No Collection Costs
findings.fact: The City shall not be obligated to pay any costs associated with your collection of an outstanding invoice.

quotes.quote: In no circumstances shall the City be obligated to pay any costs associated with your collection of an outstanding invoice.

findings.title: No Partial Payment for Commodities
findings.fact: Payment for partial delivery will not be allowed except when provided for in blanket or term contracts.

quotes.quote: Payment for partial delivery will not be allowed except when provided for in blanket or term contracts.

findings.title: Single Shipping Charge for Partial Deliveries
findings.fact: Only one shipping charge will be applied in the event of partial deliveries for blanket or term contracts.

quotes.quote: Only one shipping charge will be applied in the event of partial deliveries for blanket or term contracts.

findings.title: Annual Costs for Contracts Exceeding 12 Months
findings.fact: Contracts exceeding twelve months must specify annual costs for each year.

quotes.quote: Contracts exceeding twelve months must specify annual costs for each year.

findings.title: Bids Should Be Totaled
findings.fact: Bids should be totaled so that the final cost is clearly stated, unless submitting a unit price bid.

quotes.quote: Bids SHOULD BE TOTALED so that the final cost is clearly stated (unless submitting a unit price bid), however each item should be priced individually.

findings.title: Awards May Be by Total or Individual Items
findings.fact: Awards may be made on the basis of total bid or by individual items.

quotes.quote: Awards may be made on the basis of total bid or by individual items.

findings.title: No Automatic Renewal
findings.fact: The Agreement shall not automatically renew or be extended without a writing signed by the parties.

quotes.quote: In no event shall the Agreement automatically renew or be extended without a writing signed by the parties.

findings.title: Changes Require Written Amendment
findings.fact: Changes in the terms and conditions of the Agreement, or the scope of work thereunder, may only be made by a writing signed by the parties.

quotes.quote: Changes in the terms and conditions of the Agreement, or the scope of work thereunder, may only be made by a writing signed by the parties.

findings.title: No Assignment Without Consent
findings.fact: You shall not assign your rights and obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the City.

quotes.quote: You shall not assign your rights and obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the City.

findings.title: Minimum Experience and References Required
findings.fact: Bidder must have at least five years of experience manufacturing traffic control signs and provide three municipal references demonstrating comparable work.
findings.business_implication: Bidders without the required experience and references will be disqualified, potentially limiting competition.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure your company meets the five-year experience requirement and prepare documentation for three municipal references that can verify comparable work.

quotes.quote: Bidder shall have at least five years of experience manufacturing traffic control signs and provide three municipal references demonstrating comparable work.

findings.title: Out-of-State Corporation Registration Required
findings.fact: Out-of-state corporations must qualify or register to transact business in Rhode Island in accordance with the Rhode Island Business Corporation Act.
findings.business_implication: Out-of-state bidders must complete registration in Rhode Island before bidding, which may involve additional time and costs.
findings.action_recommendation: If your company is based outside Rhode Island, initiate the registration process with the Rhode Island Secretary of State well in advance of the bid deadline.

quotes.quote: A bidder who is an out-of-state corporation shall qualify or register to transact business in this State, in accordance with the Rhode Island Business Corporation Act, RIGL Sec. 7-1.2-1401, et seq.

findings.title: Non-Discrimination Certification Required
findings.fact: Bidder must certify that it does not unlawfully discriminate and that all employees are lawfully employed.
findings.business_implication: Failure to comply with non-discrimination and employment laws could lead to disqualification or legal liability.
findings.action_recommendation: Review your company's hiring and employment practices to ensure compliance, and be prepared to sign the certification (Bid Form 2) as part of the bid submission.

quotes.quote: Bidder must certify that it does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation and/or religion in its business and hiring practices and that all of its employees are lawfully employed under all applicable federal, state and local laws, rules and regulations. (See Bid Form 2.)

findings.title: Local Agent for Service of Process Required for Out-of-State Bidders
findings.fact: If the bidder's company is based in a state other than Rhode Island, they must list name and contact information for a local agent for service of process located within Rhode Island.
findings.business_implication: Out-of-state bidders must appoint a local agent in Rhode Island to receive legal documents, which may involve additional administrative arrangements.
findings.action_recommendation: Identify and appoint a registered agent in Rhode Island, and include their name and contact information in the bid form as required.

quotes.quote: If the bidder’s company is based in a state other than Rhode Island, list name and contact information for a local agent for service of process that is located within Rhode Island

findings.title: Disqualification for Submitting Sensitive Information Directly to Issuing Department
findings.fact: Bidders who submit sensitive information directly to the issuing department to protect pricing terms from becoming public will be disqualified.
findings.business_implication: Attempting to bypass the public bidding process by sending sensitive information directly to the issuing department will result in automatic disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Submit all required information through the official bidding process as instructed, and do not attempt to send sensitive information directly to the issuing department.

quotes.quote: Bidders who make such an attempt will be disqualified.

findings.title: Disqualification for Failure to Provide Supplemental Information
findings.fact: Failure to provide supplemental information requested by the issuing department may lead to disqualification of the bid.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must be prepared to promptly provide additional documentation (e.g., Business Tax ID, Proof of Insurance, Certificate of Good Standing) upon request after being selected as the best-suited bidder. Failure to do so can result in disqualification, even if the initial bid was successful.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all required supplemental documents are readily available and up-to-date before bid submission. Designate a point of contact to respond quickly to any requests from the issuing department.

quotes.quote: An inability to provide the outlined items at the request of the department may lead to the disqualification of your bid.

findings.title: MBE/WBE Waiver Form Required for Award Recommendation
findings.fact: City Department Directors should not recommend a bidder for an award if the MBE/WBE waiver form is not included, absent, or not signed by the MBE/WBE director.
findings.business_implication: If the bidder does not meet the 20% MBE/WBE participation goal, they must submit a waiver request form signed by the MBE/WBE director. Without this, the bidder cannot be recommended for award, potentially losing the contract.
findings.action_recommendation: If the MBE/WBE participation goal is not met, complete the waiver request form and submit it to the MBE/WBE Outreach Director for signature before bid submission. Ensure the signed form is included in the bid package.

quotes.quote: In case a waiver is needed, City Department Directors should not recommend a bidder for an award if this form is not included, absent or is not signed by the city of Providence MBE/WBE director.

findings.title: MBE/WBE Certification Required at Time of Bid
findings.fact: All MBE/WBE subcontractors/suppliers must be certified by the Office of Diversity, Equity and Opportunity at the time of bid.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure that any MBE/WBE subcontractors or suppliers listed in the bid are certified by the Office of Diversity, Equity and Opportunity at the time of bid submission. Using non-certified firms could invalidate the MBE/WBE participation and jeopardize the bid's compliance.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify the certification status of all intended MBE/WBE subcontractors/suppliers before bid submission. Use the City's MBE/WBE Directory to confirm certification and maintain documentation.

quotes.quote: Please note that all MBE/WBE subcontractors/suppliers must be certified by the Office of Diversity, Equity and Opportunity at the time of bid.

findings.title: Apprentice Requirements for Construction Projects
findings.fact: Construction projects valued at $100,000 or more must utilize not less than 15% of total hours worked by apprentices.
findings.business_implication: For construction projects over $100,000, the bidder must commit to using apprentices for at least 15% of total work hours. Non-compliance may affect payment and contract execution.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan to meet the apprentice requirement by identifying apprenticeship programs and incorporating the necessary labor hours into the project plan. Attend the mandatory meeting post-award to understand reporting requirements.

quotes.quote: This ordinance outlines requirements for utilizing not less than 15% of total hours worked by apprentices.

findings.title: First Source Requirements for Construction Projects
findings.fact: Construction projects must comply with the City's First Source Ordinance requiring hiring Providence residents.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must make a good faith effort to hire Providence residents for the project. Non-compliance may affect payment and contract execution.
findings.action_recommendation: Develop a hiring plan that prioritizes Providence residents. Be prepared to submit compliance reports with payment requisitions and attend the mandatory post-award meeting to review requirements.

quotes.quote: This ordinance outlines requirements for hiring Providence residents to work on this project.

findings.title: Bid Opening Date and Time
findings.fact: The bid opening is scheduled for July 27, 2026 at 2:15 PM.
findings.business_implication: This is the absolute deadline for bid submission. Bids must be received by the City Clerk's office before this time to be considered. Late bids will likely be rejected.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure your bid is delivered to the Department of the City Clerk, Room 311, City Hall, 25 Dorrance Street, Providence, RI 02903, before 2:15 PM on July 27, 2026. Plan for potential delays and consider hand-delivering or using a courier with tracking.

quotes.quote: Date to be opened: 7/27/2026
Meeting Date: 7/27/2026
Bids may be submitted up to 2:15 P.M. on the above meeting date at the Department of the City Clerk.

findings.title: Deadline for Questions
findings.fact: Questions must be submitted via email by July 20, 2026 at 4:00 PM (EST).
findings.business_implication: This is the last opportunity to seek clarification on the RFP. Any questions submitted after this deadline may not be answered, potentially leaving ambiguities unresolved.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the RFP thoroughly and submit all questions via email to purchasing@providenceri.gov with the subject line 'Solicitation Question' before the deadline. Ensure your questions are clear and specific to avoid misunderstandings.

quotes.quote: Deadline for questions submissions: via email by July 20, 2026 at 4:00 PM (EST).

findings.title: Award within 90 days of bid opening
findings.fact: Awards will be made within ninety (90) days of bid opening.
findings.business_implication: The City expects to make an award decision within 90 days after bid opening. This means your bid prices must remain firm for at least that period, and you should be prepared for a potential award notification around that time.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure your pricing is valid for at least 90 days after the bid opening date. Monitor communications from the City for any award notifications or requests for additional information during this period.

quotes.quote: Awards will be made within nighty (90) days of bid opening.

findings.title: Bid opening date referenced on page 1
findings.fact: The bid opening date is noted on page 1 of the RFP.
findings.business_implication: This confirms that the bid opening date is a critical reference point for the submission deadline and other timelines. It also indicates that certain information (like licenses) is not required in the initial bid but may be requested later.
findings.action_recommendation: Note the bid opening date (July 27, 2026) as the key deadline. Prepare your bid accordingly, and be ready to provide additional documentation (e.g., licenses, insurance) upon request after the award is approved.

quotes.quote: This information is NOT requested to be provided in your initial bid that you will submit to the City Clerk’s office by the “date to be opened” noted on page 1.

findings.title: Lowest Responsive and Responsible Bidder
findings.fact: Award shall be made to the lowest responsive and responsible bidder based on aggregate evaluated price and other factors.
findings.business_implication: The award is not solely based on price; the City will also evaluate the bidder's responsibility, delivery capability, product quality, warranty, references, and compliance with specifications. This means a bidder with a slightly higher price but better quality or service could win.
findings.action_recommendation: Emphasize your company's strengths in these areas in your bid. Provide strong references, demonstrate reliable delivery capabilities, and highlight product quality and warranty terms. Ensure your bid is fully compliant with all specifications to be considered responsive.

quotes.quote: Award shall be made to the lowest responsive and responsible bidder based on the aggregate evaluated price and the bidder's demonstrated responsibility, delivery capability, product quality, warranty, references, and compliance with the specifications.

findings.title: Award to lowest qualified and responsible bidder
findings.fact: The Board of Contract and Supply will make the award to the lowest qualified and responsible bidder.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must be both the lowest price and meet all qualification criteria to win the contract. Price is a key factor, but not the only one.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure the bid is competitive in price while also demonstrating compliance with all requirements and qualifications.

quotes.quote: The Board of Contract and Supply will make the award to the lowest qualified and responsible bidder.

findings.title: Right to reject any and all bids
findings.fact: The Board of Contract and Supply reserves the right to reject any and all bids.
findings.business_implication: Even if the bidder submits a compliant bid, the City may reject all bids, meaning there is no guarantee of award.
findings.action_recommendation: Submit the best possible bid, but be aware that the City may reject all bids and re-solicit.

quotes.quote: The Board of Contract and Supply reserves the right to reject any and all bids.

findings.title: Failure to provide supplemental information may result in disqualification
findings.fact: The requested supplemental information may be crucial to evaluating bids. Failure to provide such details may result in disqualification, or an inability to appropriately evaluate bids.
findings.business_implication: Incomplete submissions can lead to disqualification or poor evaluation, risking the bid.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully review all supplemental information requirements and ensure all requested details are provided in the bid.

quotes.quote: The requested supplemental information may be crucial to evaluating bids. Failure to provide such details may result in disqualification, or an inability to appropriately evaluate bids.

findings.title: Bidders who submit sensitive information directly to issuing department will be disqualified
findings.fact: The City of Providence observes a public and transparent bidding process. Information required in the bidding packet may not be submitted directly to the issuing department at the discretion of the bidder in order to protect other information, such as pricing terms, from becoming public. Bidders who make such an attempt will be disqualified.
findings.business_implication: Attempting to submit required information directly to the issuing department to keep it confidential will result in automatic disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Submit all required information through the official bidding process to the City Clerk; do not attempt to bypass the process.

quotes.quote: The City of Providence observes a public and transparent bidding process. Information required in the bidding packet may not be submitted directly to the issuing department at the discretion of the bidder in order to protect other information, such as pricing terms, from becoming public. Bidders who make such an attempt will be disqualified.

findings.title: Firm Fixed Unit Price Contract
findings.fact: The contract is a firm fixed unit price contract with prices firm for the initial term, subject to renewal adjustments.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must commit to fixed unit prices for the initial term, bearing the risk of cost increases; however, renewal adjustments may allow for price changes.
findings.action_recommendation: Price the bid carefully to cover all costs for the initial term, and consider potential cost escalations; also, understand the renewal adjustment mechanism.

quotes.quote: The Contractor shall provide all awarded items at the fixed unit prices submitted in its bid for the duration of the initial contract term. Unit prices shall include all labor, materials, manufacturing, packaging, freight, delivery, overhead, profit, and all other costs necessary to furnish the requested items. Except as otherwise provided for approved renewal-term price adjustments, unit prices shall remain firm throughout the contract term.

findings.title: Purchase Order Required
findings.fact: No goods should be delivered or work started without a Purchase Order.
findings.business_implication: The City will not accept or pay for any goods or services provided without a valid Purchase Order. This means the bidder must ensure that a Purchase Order is issued and received before commencing any work or delivery, to avoid non-payment and potential disputes.
findings.action_recommendation: Before starting any work or delivering goods, confirm that a Purchase Order has been issued by the City and is in hand. Keep a copy of the Purchase Order for records and reference it in all communications and invoices.

quotes.quote: No goods should be delivered, or work started without a Purchase Order.

findings.title: Payment Terms: 60 Days
findings.fact: Invoices submitted to the City shall be payable sixty (60) days from the time of receipt by the City.
findings.business_implication: The City will pay invoices 60 days after receipt, which may impact the bidder's cash flow. The bidder should plan for a 60-day payment cycle and ensure that invoices are complete and accurate to avoid delays in payment.
findings.action_recommendation: Submit invoices promptly with all required supporting documentation to ensure the 60-day clock starts. Monitor accounts receivable and follow up with the City's finance department if payment is not received within the expected timeframe.

quotes.quote: Invoices submitted to the City shall be payable sixty (60) days from the time of receipt by the City.

findings.title: Firm Prices for 90 Days
findings.fact: All bid prices will be considered firm for 90 days after bid opening, and requests for price increases will not be honored.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must hold its quoted prices for at least 90 days after bid opening. This means the bidder cannot increase prices during this period, even if costs rise, and must factor in potential cost fluctuations when preparing the bid.
findings.action_recommendation: When preparing the bid, ensure that the quoted prices are sustainable for at least 90 days. Consider including a contingency for potential cost increases and avoid submitting prices that may become unprofitable if costs rise.

quotes.quote: Awards will be made within nighty (90) days of bid opening. All bid prices will be considered firm, unless qualified otherwise. Requests for price increases will not be honored.

findings.title: Bid Prices in Writing and Figures
findings.fact: Bid prices must be stated both in writing and in figures, and proposals not so stated may be rejected.
findings.business_implication: The bid must include the total price in both written words and numerical figures. Failure to do so may result in the bid being rejected, even if the price is otherwise correct.
findings.action_recommendation: Double-check the bid form to ensure that the total amount is written out in words and also provided in figures. Have a second person review the bid before submission to avoid any oversight.

quotes.quote: The price or prices proposed should be stated both in WRITING and in FIGURES, and any proposal not so stated may be rejected.

findings.title: Entire Agreement and Supersession
findings.fact: The RFP and Standard Terms and Conditions constitute the entire agreement and supersede any conflicting provisions provided by bid.
findings.business_implication: By submitting a bid, the bidder agrees to the City's Standard Terms and Conditions, which override any conflicting terms in the bidder's own proposal. This means the bidder cannot rely on its own terms that contradict the City's terms.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the City's Standard Terms and Conditions carefully before bidding. If any of the bidder's standard terms conflict, be prepared to accept the City's terms or consider whether to bid at all. Ensure that any exceptions or modifications are clearly noted in the bid as required.

quotes.quote: The Request For Proposals (“RFP”) and these Standard Terms and Conditions together constitute the entire agreement of the parties (“the Agreement”) with regard to any and all matters. By your submission of a bid proposal or response to the City’s RFP, you accept these Standard Terms & Conditions and agree that they supersede any conflicting provisions provided by bid or in any terms and conditions contained or linked within a bid and/or response.

findings.title: Prevailing Wage and First Source Apply
findings.fact: For construction contracts, applicable state labor law concerning prevailing wage rates and the City’s First Source Ordinance apply.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must comply with state prevailing wage laws and the City's First Source Ordinance, which may increase labor costs and require additional administrative efforts to ensure compliance.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the specific wage rates and First Source requirements, factor them into the bid pricing, and prepare to provide necessary documentation and reports.

quotes.quote: For contracts involving construction, alteration, and/or repair work, the provisions of applicable state labor law concerning payment of prevailing wage rates (R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 37-13-1 et seq., as amended) and the City’s First Source Ordinance (Providence Code of Ordinances §§ 21-91 et seq., as amended) apply.

findings.title: Unlimited Indemnification Obligation
findings.fact: The contractor must indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the City from any and all claims, damages, losses, etc., arising out of the performance of the work, with no stated limitation.
findings.business_implication: The contractor assumes potentially unlimited liability for any claims arising from the work, which could lead to significant financial exposure beyond the contract value.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess the risk and consider obtaining comprehensive insurance coverage, including professional liability if applicable, and consult legal counsel to understand the full scope of the indemnification obligation.

quotes.quote: To the fullest extent permitted by law, you shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the City, its employees, officers, agents, and assigns from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, allegations, demands, actions, causes of action, suits, obligations, fines, penalties, judgments, liabilities, costs and expenses, including but not limited to attorneys’ fees, of any nature whatsoever arising out of, in connection with, or resulting from the performance of the work provided in the Agreement.

findings.title: No Limitation of Liability for Contractor
findings.fact: The City does not agree to limit the contractor's liability to the contract price or any other monetary limit.
findings.business_implication: The contractor's liability is not capped, meaning potential damages could exceed the contract value, increasing financial risk.
findings.action_recommendation: Evaluate the risk and consider negotiating for a limitation of liability clause, or ensure adequate insurance coverage to mitigate potential losses.

quotes.quote: The City shall not subject itself to any contractual limitations on liability. The City shall have the time permitted within the applicable statute of limitations, and no less, to bring or assert any and all causes of action, suits, claims or demands the City may have arising out of, in connection with, or resulting from the performance of the work provided in the Agreement, and in no event does the City agree to limit your liability to the price of the Agreement or any other monetary limit.

findings.title: City Not Subject to Dispute Resolution
findings.fact: The City is not required to submit to dispute resolution or mandatory/binding arbitration.
findings.business_implication: Disputes may have to be resolved in court, which can be more time-consuming and costly than arbitration, and the contractor may have less leverage in dispute resolution.
findings.action_recommendation: Be prepared for potential litigation and consider including dispute resolution mechanisms in the contract if possible, or factor in legal costs when pricing the bid.

quotes.quote: With regard to any issues, claims, or controversies that may arise under this Agreement, the City shall not be required to submit to dispute resolution or mandatory/binding arbitration.

findings.title: Insurance Requirements
findings.fact: The contractor must maintain insurance coverage as required by the RFP or commercially reasonable, and name the City as an additional insured on general liability and umbrella policies.
findings.business_implication: The contractor must secure and maintain adequate insurance coverage, which adds to the cost of the project, and must ensure the City is named as an additional insured, which may increase premiums.
findings.action_recommendation: Obtain insurance quotes early, ensure the coverage meets the requirements, and budget for the additional costs. Verify that the additional insured endorsement is included.

quotes.quote: You shall maintain throughout the term of this Agreement the insurance coverage that is required by the RFP or, if none is required in the RFP, insurance coverage that is considered in your industry to be commercially reasonable, and you agree to name the City as an additional insured on your general liability policy and on any umbrella policy you carry.

findings.title: Data Breach Notification Obligation
findings.fact: The contractor must notify the City within 24 hours of discovering a breach of confidential or personal information.
findings.business_implication: The contractor must have robust incident detection and response procedures to ensure any breach is identified and reported to the City within 24 hours. Failure to comply could result in contractual penalties, loss of trust, and potential legal liability.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement a breach response plan that includes immediate internal escalation and a clear communication channel to the City's designated contact. Train staff on breach identification and reporting requirements. Consider cyber insurance to mitigate potential costs.

quotes.quote: In the event of a breach of such information, you shall notify the City of such breach immediately, but in no event later than twenty-four (24) hours after discovery of such breach.

findings.title: Governing Law and Venue
findings.fact: The agreement is governed by Rhode Island law, and all actions must occur in Rhode Island state or federal court.
findings.business_implication: The contractor must be prepared to litigate any disputes in Rhode Island, which may be inconvenient and costly if the contractor is not located in the state. Understanding Rhode Island law is essential.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess the cost and practicality of litigating in Rhode Island. Consider consulting with local counsel to understand the implications. If the contractor is not based in Rhode Island, factor in potential travel and legal fees.

quotes.quote: The Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Rhode Island. You expressly submit yourself to and agree that any and all actions arising out of, in connection with, or resulting from the performance of the Agreement or relationship between the parties shall occur solely in the venue and jurisdiction of the State of Rhode Island or the federal court located in Rhode Island.

findings.title: Conflict in Financial Assurance Requirements
findings.fact: The Bid Terms section lists multiple financial assurance options (a, b, c, d) but does not specify which one applies to this IFB. The Bid Package Checklist says financial assurance is required only if specified on page 12, but page 12 does not indicate which option is checked. This creates ambiguity.
findings.business_implication: The ambiguity creates uncertainty about whether the bidder must provide a financial assurance and in what form. This could lead to bid disqualification if the wrong assumption is made, or unnecessary costs if a bond is posted when not required.
findings.action_recommendation: Seek clarification from the City's purchasing department before submitting the bid. If clarification is not possible, consider including a bid bond or certified check as a precaution, but weigh the cost. Alternatively, submit the bid without financial assurance and note the ambiguity, but be aware of the risk of disqualification.

quotes.quote: Financial assurances may be required in order to be a successful bidder for Commodity or Construction and Service contracts. If either of the first two checkboxes below is checked, the specified assurance must accompany a bid, or the bid will not be considered by the Board of Contract and Supply. The third checkbox indicates the lowest responsible bidder will be contacted and required to post a bond to be awarded the contract. a) A certified check for $ must be deposited with the City Clerk as a guarantee that the Contract will be signed and delivered by the bidder. b) A bid bond in the amount of per centum (%) of the proposed total price, must be deposited with the City Clerk as a guarantee that the contract will be signed and delivered by the bidder; and the amount of such bid bond shall be retained for the use of the City as liquidated damages in case of default. Any person signing a bid bond as an attorney-in-fact shall include with the bid bond an original, or a photocopy or facsimile of an original, power of attorney. c) A performance and payment bond with a satisfactory surety company will be posted by the bidder in a sum equal to one hundred per centum (100%) of the awarded contract. d) No financial assurance is necessary for this item.
Financial Assurance, if requested (as indicated on page 5 of this document under “Bid Terms”)

findings.title: Conflict in Installation Services Completion Times
findings.fact: Section 8 states 'Routine Work: Five (5) business days after receipt of a work order' but the Standard Terms and Conditions do not specify installation times. However, there is no direct contradiction, but the ambiguity is that the installation services are optional and may not be awarded, yet the completion times are specified.
findings.business_implication: The contractor must be prepared to meet the specified completion times if installation services are awarded, but the optional nature of the services means the contractor may not need to allocate resources unless the City exercises the option. The ambiguity could lead to disputes over expectations.
findings.action_recommendation: Clarify with the City whether the installation services will be awarded and under what conditions. Ensure that the bid pricing for installation services accounts for the required completion times and any associated costs. If the services are optional, consider including contingency plans for meeting the deadlines.

quotes.quote: Unless otherwise authorized, installation work shall be completed within: • Routine Work: Five (5) business days after receipt of a work order. • Priority Work: Forty-eight (48) hours. • Emergency Work: Twenty-four (24) hours.

At the City's option, the Contractor may also provide sign installation services as described in Section 7A (Optional Add/Alternate Sign Installation Services). Installation services shall not be included in the base bid and shall only be performed when specifically authorized by the City through a purchase order or work authorization.
